newsitem.title: USA: Champion Q2 EPS could fall below $0.39.
newsitem.headline: Champion Q2 EPS could fall below $0.39.

text.p: Champion Enterprises Inc, a manufactured housing company, said Thursday its second quarter earnings could fall below the $0.39 a share reported a year ago.
"...current market conditions and higher operating costs could result in earnings below last year's $0.39 per share," chief executive Walter Young Jr. said in a news release.

Young also said the 2.4 percent decline in year-to-date wholesale shipments for the industry through April make it unlikely for industry growth for the full year to be as high as the four to seven percent increase the company had previously estimated.
He also said low backlogs increase operaitng costs, making it difficult to accurately predict margins and earnings for the full year and quarter.
"We had based our calendar 1997 EPS estimate of $1.62 to $1.67 on increases in industry shipments of four to seven percent," he said.

"As we stated at the end of the first quarter, higher dealer inventory levels due to weather and other factors must be reduced before wholesale shipments will improve," he said. "Indications suggest that retail inventories continue to shrink and that retail sales are up. However, given the wholesale shipments year-to-date, current Wall Street estimates for the industry range from down two percent to up five percent for this year," he said.
